text:
My neighbor, in a fit of dramatic flair, put up a sign that read "Beware of Dog." It was meant to be intimidating, but the reality was a three-pound furball who weighed less than a loaf of sourdough bread. When the postman arrived, my tiny terror charged out, barking with the ferocity of a lion, only to trip over his own paws and land with a soft *poof*. The postman, clearly unimpressed by the threat level, sighed and said, "Oh no, I'm so scared!"

That comment broke my dog. He took it as a personal challenge. Now, he’s on a relentless mission to prove the postman wrong. He doesn’t just bark anymore; he practices tactical maneuvers. He’s started staring intensely at the mailbox, calculating trajectories. Yesterday, he tried to "attack" a leaf blowing across the yard with such vigor that he spun in circles until he got dizzy and fell over. The postman still isn’t scared, but he does leave an extra treat in the box now, probably out of pity for my dog’s failing stealth skills. I’m pretty sure my dog is currently plotting his next move, and I’m just waiting for the day he decides to take on the vacuum cleaner.
